title: Trigger graph: auto-grow value textareas and stop the inspector triggers header overflowing

sections.what: Trigger-graph value textareas are fixed rows=2 and scroll instead of growing with their content, and the inspector triggers-section header packs five buttons into one nowrap row that clips on a narrow panel. Make textareas grow to fit their value, and let the button row wrap.
sections.why: Fixed-height trigger parameter textareas forced continuous scrolling and trigger headers overflowed on narrow viewports.
sections.how: Added auto-expanding textarea behavior matching content height and wrapped trigger headers using responsive flexbox rules.
sections.verify:
1. Type multiline text into trigger effect parameter
   - expected: Textarea auto-expands to fit text without vertical scrollbars
   - observed: Auto-grow behavior verified in trigger editor

acceptance.text: A trigger-graph value textarea grows to fit its content as it is typed (no inner scrollbar for a long message/instructions).
A textarea with an existing long value is sized on open and on every node re-render.
The inspector triggers header's five buttons wrap instead of clipping on a narrow panel (`flex-wrap` on the header and button row).
Live: open the trigger graph, type a multi-line message, confirm the box grows; narrow the inspector and confirm the header buttons wrap.
(2026-10-16 live on :4444: `_autoGrow` measured on a real
`textarea.tg-field` - 36px scrolling → 52px grown, no scrollbar;
node render calls `_sizeTextareas` after every render
(`trigger-graph.js:1632`); typing grows via the delegated canvas
`input` listener (same proven function). Header wrap is
source-verified (`flex-wrap` on header + button row,
`trigger-helpers.js:152/154`) but has no narrow-panel screenshot
yet. Retraction note: an early "unsized textarea" sighting was my
own synthetic-test litter (a canvas-child textarea without
`data-key`), not app UI - removed, and the real node path sizes
on render.)
Observed 2026-10-16 (Playwright, headless Chromium, http://localhost:4444, item `belt_leather`
via `VW.inspector.showNode`): the Triggers header holds 5 buttons. At the default inspector
width (379px) they sit on 2 rows, none clipped. With `#inspector-panel` forced to 260px they sit
on 2 rows, none outside the panel, header `scrollWidth` equals its width (228). Control: forcing
`flex-wrap:nowrap` on the header and button row at 260px gives 1 row, `scrollWidth` 415 against
228 and 3 buttons outside the panel (Suggest, Suggest (AI), Add), so the check does detect
clipping. Limit: the panel width was set by style, not by dragging the real resizer.

custom.notes:
Implemented in `static/js/shared/trigger-graph.ts` (`_autoGrow` / `_sizeTextareas`,
delegated `input` listener on `#tg-canvas`, sizing after `_renderNode`) and
`static/js/inspector/trigger-helpers.ts` (wrap styles on the header row).
Rebuilt with `npm run build:ts`.

Gate: `ts_convert.py check` - build/typecheck/lint/unit/headers/window-guards all
ok; only the pre-existing `module:check` failure on `engine/activities_loader.py`
and `engine/effect_handlers/movement.py` remains (unrelated, py module headers).

Still unimplemented from the same recon: a left-to-right stacking-siblings graph
layout for the trigger graph - it needs a decision first, since condition
`output_yes`/`output_no` sockets are `side:'bottom'` and are compile-coupled.
custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Trigger Graph value fields and Character/Area Inspector → Triggers section header.

Current availability: Textarea growth and wrapped inspector controls are partly implemented; remaining live acceptance is open.

Live steps when available:

1. Open Trigger Graph, type a multiline value, then reopen a node with a long saved value.
   - expected: The textarea grows to its content on input and render without an internal scrollbar.

2. Narrow the Inspector and inspect the Triggers header.
   - expected: Buttons wrap within the panel instead of clipping or forcing horizontal overflow.

This section defines the intended access point and acceptance path. It is not a claim that the UI or complete behavior exists or works today; Current availability records the present state, and these steps describe how to verify the intended behavior when it is available.
